tilts.set: SET on 2026-11-06 by the Portfolio Fitness for Fighting judg

industry.why: Neutral, carried, split. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): DNB Carnegie's new mining cycle and Danske's soft commodities up 10 to 40% since the second quarter are the demand side; Metals and mining relative strength falling to F from A, steel to D from B and cement to F from C are the tape, with energy costs at Brent $111 the margin squeeze. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: D now, C prior. Base chemicals, Steel and Cement carry D; Fragrances, Specialty chemicals and Forestry stay C.

sector.why: Underweight, from Neutral. Component 1 regime, 9-Oct-26 (late-cycle rates squeeze turning into a European credit-and-sovereign stress episode: hiking path re-marked up, credit joined rates, French spread 152 basis points, European breadth at three-year lows on all four averages, index 5.3% off its high, defensives turning over one and four weeks but unconfirmed, growth firm at the level; sources present 2026-W41): two houses now name construction as the rate casualty: DNB Carnegie (8 Oct) has logistics and construction customers postponing investment with European construction under pressure, and Goldman Sachs (5 Oct) has residential investment taking the heaviest hit from higher rates; the turning note's falling side adds United Kingdom housebuilders and lifting equipment as whole groups. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-09 against 2026-08-07, not week on week: construction and infrastructure contractors D now from C, cement and aggregates F now from D, so the tape agrees. Counter-case: 57 stocks of mixed character, infrastructure and defence-funded spending supports part of them, and rate-sensitive groups are the most oversold in five years (Daily Chartbook, 3 Oct), which is where a rates relief rally starts; back to C if the Fed path is marked down again.

geography.why: Neutral, carried; the re-test written last week (Neutral against Underweight after the Bank of England's decision and guidance on 5-Nov-26) could not run, because no source in the pack reports the outcome; the only United Kingdom items are undated headlines (the pound firmer on policy divergence; shoppers 'more upbeat than their European counterparts', City AM, against a GfK 'weakens in November' headline most likely from 2025). Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). The Budget read of last week stands: a UK-specific fiscal tail risk removed without lowering the rate; 22 of the Pool stocks are UK-listed and a Neutral country carries no weight in Thematic Fit/Momentum. Counter-case unchanged: a 1.0% growth year with a hiking central bank is an Underweight in most books. To D on hawkish guidance when the 5-Nov-26 decision is read, a January price cap above 16% or a spring fiscal event with broad taxes; to B if a second source makes the UK case with the rate path read.

beta.method: Dimson: same-day plus previous-day market slopes, daily returns, last 252 common days, Stoxx Europe 600

experiment.label: Experiment
experiment.method: own daily moves (Stoxx Europe 600 and country-of-listing average removed), rank correlation, last 63 and 126 sessions; candidates EUR 500m or more in the same sector, cohort or country of listing

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
